_comment: Classes below the coverage bar, accepted as existing debt. Every entry carries a reason, and the build fails on one that does not - accepting debt is a decision, not a keystroke. The build also fails if a class goes further backwards, or if a class arrives below the bar and is not listed here. "excluded" is the separate list of classes the report does not measure at all: a baselined class that vanishes from the report is not a class that was fixed, and without that list it could leave the ledger by ceasing to be measured. Regenerate with build/check-coverage.ps1 -UpdateBaseline, then write a reason for anything new and review the diff.

MLQT.McpServer::MLQT.McpServer.Helpers.C.reason: 1.1 points under the bar. The gap is the splice paths for class shapes no fixture builds yet. Reachable; not yet written.

MLQT.McpServer::MLQT.McpServer.Helpers.E.reason: 0.6 points under the bar. The gap is the ambiguous- and not-found-entity branches. Reachable; not yet written.

MLQT.McpServer::MLQT.McpServer.Services..reason: Writes a usage log to disk. The gap is the IO-failure branches, which the logger swallows by design so a logging fault cannot fail a tool call. Reachable with a locked file; not yet written.

MLQT.McpServer::MLQT.McpServer.Tools.Sup.reason: Phase 5c's authoring path. The covered half is the tool contract; the gap is the failure branches (unwritable file, class not found, malformed rule id). Reachable; not yet written.

MLQT.Services::MLQT.Services.DymolaCheck.reason: Talks to a running Dymola over HTTP JSON-RPC. No licence and no install on a runner; the parsing and error paths are covered, the conversation is not. The figure is stable rather than flaky, and that took a fix: StartCheckingAsync_WhenAlreadyRunning_DoesNotStartAgain only attempted its second call `if (service.IsRunning)`, which was usually false by then, so the early return in StartCheckingAsync was covered about one run in four. The test now holds the first check open at a gate, so that line is reached every time. It rose from 34.2 with B259/B260, which added both lines and tests here.

MLQT.Services::MLQT.Services.Helpers.For.reason: 25%, and new debt this branch created rather than inherited: 7a-4 moved both formatting paths here out of MainLayout. FormatChangedFilesAsync and FormatModifiedFilesAsync are tested against a temp directory, and the decisions inside the full save are tested separately (IncrementalFormatter, OrphanedFileSelector, ResolveSaveDirectory, EmptyDirectoryCleaner, FileNodeReconciler). What is uncovered is the 250-line sequencing of SaveAllLibrariesWithFormattingAsync itself, which needs a library on disk with a real file layout to restructure - a fixture, not a mock. Worth writing: it is the path Format All Files takes.

MLQT.Services::MLQT.Services.OpenModelic.reason: Talks to a running OpenModelica over ZeroMQ. Same reason as DymolaCheckingService. Stable rather than flaky for the same reason as DymolaCheckingService - see its entry - and up from 34 with B259/B260, which changed both services together.

MLQT.Shared::MLQT.Shared.Components.Libr.reason: The tree building, the lazy-load selection regression, the reference-only labelling and the change markers are covered, all by bUnit tests written for them specifically - B200 added the repository-mode render, which moved this from 22% to 34%, and B191's markers and change filter took it to 48.5%. The rest is VCS operation UI - refresh, switch branch, merge, commit - which opens dialogs and needs a working copy.

MLQT.Shared::MLQT.Shared.Components.Nami.reason: 36%: the pattern validation is tested, which is the part that can accept something that later throws. The rest is the MudBlazor select and the pattern list's add/remove.

What is left here is orchestration that needs a render tree - the file picker, the snackbar, the re-render and the scroll restoration around each action - which the Layer 2 journeys cover and which a unit test could only assert mocks for.

MLQT.Shared::MLQT.Shared.Pages.SelfTest.reason: Every probe is a call into JS interop or a platform service, so the class does nothing measurable without a host. It is covered where it can be: 5 journeys drive the route through a real browser against MLQT.TestHost, and the committed MAUI baseline is its output from the real app. Neither suite is in the coverage merge. Raising this would mean testing the probes against fakes, which would assert that the fakes work and is the opposite of what the route is for.

ModelicaParser::ModelicaParser.ExternalD.reason: Reads a vendor's generated help HTML. Covered against the shapes Dymola 2024x emits; the gap is the malformed-input branches, which need fixtures nobody has captured a real example of.

ModelicaParser::ModelicaParser.Helpers.M.reason: 1.9 points under the bar. The uncovered lines are the rarer BOM and Latin-1 fallback combinations. Reachable from a fixture file; not yet written.
Not yet tested to the parser assembly's 95% bar: the uncovered lines are the error-recovery and diagnostic-formatting branches reached only by malformed input. Reachable; nobody has written them.

ModelicaParser::ModelicaParser.StyleRule.reason: 2 points under the bar, and deliberately. B175 added the removal half of the writer, whose uncovered lines are two `Parse(...) is null` guards: one before the splice and one re-parsing the result. Neither is reachable from these entry points - the parser recovers rather than returning nothing - but the second is the backstop on a method that rewrites a class's source rather than adding to it, and removing a safety net to move a number is the wrong trade. The rest of the class is the older debt: splice positions for annotation shapes no fixture yet produces.

RevisionControl::RevisionControl.SvnCli.reason: Drives the svn executable. Same reason as SvnRevisionControlSystem: no svn on the runner. **This figure has to come from a CI run, not from a developer machine.** How much of this class is covered depends on whether an svn client is on PATH, not on which tests ran: the Code Coverage job is windows-latest with no svn installed, and a machine that has one covers roughly twice as much. Re-recording the baseline locally put this at 51.5% and the gate then failed on CI at 27.3%, which is what the warning in check-coverage.ps1 now exists to stop.

RevisionControl::RevisionControl.SvnRevi.reason: Needs a real SVN working copy and a server; the suite that covers it (SvnOperationsTests) is filtered out of the CI run for that reason. Covered locally against C:\Projects\ModelicaEditorTest.

RevisionControl::RevisionControl.SvnTool.reason: Finds an installed svn. There is none on the runner, so every branch that matters is the not-found one. **This figure has to come from a CI run, not from a developer machine.** How much of this class is covered depends on whether an svn client is on PATH, not on which tests ran: the Code Coverage job is windows-latest with no svn installed, and a machine that has one covers roughly twice as much. Re-recording the baseline locally put this at 75% and the gate then failed on CI at 71.8%, which is what the warning in check-coverage.ps1 now exists to stop.

MLQT.McpServer::Program.reason: Not in the coverage report at all, and correctly so: Program.cs is top-level statements, so the class is compiler-generated, and coverlet.MTP excludes generated code the way this script's header already says it wants. It was measured at 0% under coverlet.collector and carried as debt with the reason 'the stdio host: DI wiring and a blocking server loop, exercised by running the server - MLQT.McpTester and dev/smoke.sh - not by a unit test', which is still true. Listed here rather than dropped, because a class leaving the ledger by ceasing to be measured is exactly what B104 was.
